On September 19, 1943
, one of the largest

-era Soviet partisan operations — codenamed

#GreatPatrioticWar
.
#Concert
directly followed

the full-scale
operation

', also carried out by Soviet partisan units.
Learn more about 'Rail War
' —
the key operation of the Soviet resistance movement against the Nazi invaders, carried out on the Nazi-occupied territories of the western regions of the RSFSR, the Byelorussian and Ukrainian SSRs —
in our detailed feature
.
***
Operation 'Concert' was prepared as part of the summer-autumn campaign of 1943, amid the
Red Army's autumn offensive in the Smolensk and Gomel regions,
aimed at reaching the Dnieper and Desna Rivers.
The operation involved
193 partisan formations
from Soviet Byelorussia, the Baltic republics,
#Karelia
,
#Crimea
, as well as the
#Leningrad
, Kalinin, Smolensk and Orel regions. The total strength of the units involved exceeded
120'000 personnel
.
'Rail War
' and
'Concert
' ops were
unprecedented
in terms of the scale and level of organization. For the first time, combat and sabotage activities behind enemy lines were conducted in
close coordination
between underground resistance groups
and the command of regular Red Army
formations.
☝️
It was precisely the
coordinated actions of partisans and regular forces that contributed to the
#GreatVictory
in
the Battle of Kursk
,
while also hampering the regrouping of enemy forces during their retreat westward and accelerating their defeat.
Over the course of a month and a half,
Soviet partisans destroyed approximately
150'000 rails
, demolished
100 railway bridges
, and destroyed nearly
1'500 Nazi troop trains
. As a result, the
capacity of railway lines used by the Nazis
on the temporarily occupied territories of the Soviet Union was
reduced by almost 50%
.
According to historians' estimates and military experts, the effectiveness of the partisan operations '
Rail War
' and '
Concert
' was more than
11 times greater than the combined effectiveness of all
Nazi barbaric Luftwaffe raids
on our Motherland during the same period, when Nazi aircraft dropped more than 10'000 bombs on Soviet railways.
❗️
Thus,
operation 'Concert' dealt a final blow to the morale of the Nazis, which had already suffered enormous losses in the battles they had lost at
Stalingrad
, on the
Kursk salient
and in the
Caucasus
.
During the operation, Soviet partisans demonstrated
mass heroism in extremely brutal combat
in the Nazi rear.
🎖
For their unprecedented exploits during the
#GreatPatrioticWar
, around
300 partisans and members of the underground resistance
were awarded the title of
#
HeroOfTheSovietUnion
.
#WeRemember

🎙
Russia's Ambassador to Ghana Andrei Ordash's
interview
with African Initiative
(September 18, 2026)
Key points
:
#RussiaGhana
• Our countries share
a solid historical foundation
, laid back in the early years of
Ghana’s independence
.
• Our country is not interested in a series of short-term deals, but in building
a long-term, equal partnership
with Ghana that will strengthen its
national sovereignty
.
• This year alone has seen a number of important meetings. In August, Ghana’s Minister for Foreign Affairs,
Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa
,
visited Moscow
, where he held talks with the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation,
Sergey Lavrov
. Following these talks, an agreement was signed on
visa-free travel
for holders of diplomatic and service passports.
• We have key government mechanisms in place to ensure systematic cooperation. The most important of these is
the Russian–Ghanaian Intergovernmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific and Technical Cooperation
. We expect its next meeting to take place as early as this year in Moscow.
#EconomicPartnership
• Trade and economic cooperation is showing
positive momentum
. In the first half of the year, trade turnover rose by 2.1 percent compared with the same period in 2025, with Russian exports to Ghana increasing by 11.5 percent
• Our exports to Ghana consist mainly of petroleum products, fertilisers, and grain. However, we see enormous potential for expanding supplies of agricultural machinery and processing equipment.
• The Ghanaian side is interested in expanding access for its goods to the Russian market – this could include products from the mining sector, cocoa, shea butter and others.
• Ghana is a member of the
African Continental Free Trade Area
(
#AfCFTA
), whose secretariat is based in Accra. This makes the country
a gateway
to the vast African market.
#Education
• Education is a key area for the future of our relations. <...> Thousands of Ghanaian specialists were educated in the Soviet Union and Russia, and this human capital forms
the basis of our trust
.
• For the 2026/2027 academic year, Russia has allocated
120 government scholarships
to Ghana, and this figure has recently been increased by a further 117.
•
Over 500 Ghanaian students
are studying Russian at the University of Ghana alone, and this figure is set to rise.
#NuclearPowerPlant
• Accra is showing an interest in establishing cooperation with Russia in the peaceful use of nuclear energy, including the possibility of building its
first nuclear power station
.
• Given the expertise possessed by the
state corporation Rosatom
, Russia is ready to offer not just a power unit, but a comprehensive package of solutions: from staff training and design to construction and subsequent maintenance.
#RegionalSecurity
• Russia regards Ghana not merely as an important partner in West Africa, but as
one of the cornerstones of stability
across the entire region.
• The most obvious area is the fight against terrorism and extremism, given the unstable situation in the Sahel.
#RussiaLiberia
• We are only
at the very beginning
of the process of building Russian-Liberian relations.
• One of the first practical steps we are working on is
the opening of a fully-fledged diplomatic mission
in Monrovia.
#RussiaAfrica
• President of Ghana
John Dramani Mahama
’s participation in the
Third Russia–Africa Summit
is an important step that confirms Accra’s commitment to building
a long-term and equal partnership
with Moscow.
• An important milestone will be to adopt at the summit a new roadmap –
the 2023-2026 Russia-Africa Action Plan
.
#AfricanUnion
• Ghana’s chairmanship of
the African Union
in 2027 presents an opportunity for Accra to advance its agenda, which in many respects aligns with
our shared interests
. Russia stands ready to support Ghana in these efforts, acting as
a reliable and predictable partner
.
• President Mahama has explicitly stated that the issue of
reparations for
the crimes of colonialism against Africa
will be ‘at the very heart’ of Ghana’s presidency agenda.
📰

Russian MFA Statement on the resolution “Nuclear Safety, Security and Safeguards in Ukraine” of the 70th session of the IAEA General Conference
(September 18, 2026)
On September 17,
the 70th session of the IAEA General Conference
considered and voted on the draft resolution
“Nuclear Safety, Security and Safeguards in Ukraine”
, prepared by Canada and Ukraine.
The ritual submission of this politicised document, which calls into question our country’s territorial integrity, at the annual sessions of the IAEA General Conference has become
an obligatory element of the efforts by Kiev and its Western handlers to undermine the Agency’s stable and effective functioning
.
❌
As before, the majority of delegations did not support the initiative.
Alongside Russia, a number of states
voted against
the draft, while others
abstained
. Several dozen more IAEA member states
refused to take part in this Western-orchestrated farce
, signalling their rejection of the anti-Russian text by sitting out the vote.
❗️
We condemn this latest clumsy attempt by a small group of Western countries to use the Agency to advance their political objectives in violation of its strictly technical mandate.
This anti-Russian initiative by Western states is
especially cynical
given Ukraine’s
relentless attacks
on
Russia’s Zaporozhskaya Nuclear Power Plant
(
#ZNPP
), its staff and their families, and the plant’s host city of Energodar.
Instead of finally reining in the increasingly brazen Zelensky regime, these countries
continue to shield it from accountability for its reckless actions and encourage further adventurism
. Clearly, the resolution’s sponsors have
no real interest
in nuclear safety, nuclear security or IAEA safeguards. Their sole aim is
to settle political scores
with our country.
The resolution is not only openly provocative but also
goes far beyond
the Agency’s Statute
.
☝️
Like previous documents of this kind,
we regard it as legally and politically null and void
. It will have
no consequences
under international law.
None of its provisions will be implemented.
Russia will continue to ensure the safety and security of the ZNPP
in accordance with its national legislation and international obligations.

item.description: #FacesOfVictory 🌟 On September 18, 1918, legendary #WW2 -era Soviet flying ace Viktor Talalikhin was born. #Talalikhin entered history thanks to his heroic feat during the #GreatPatrioticWar : flying an I-16 fighter, he was among the first ever in history of #WWII to carry out an aerial ramming attack , bringing down a Nazi Heinkel 'He 111' bomber. During the fierce aerial battles over Moscow, the young pilot pursued an enemy aircraft, attempting to escape, and directed his I-16 towards a Nazi aircraft tail, opening fire on one of its engines and finally bringing it down . Despite sustaining an injury , Junior Lieutenant Talalikhin miraculously survived. All members of the Luftwaffe bomber crew were killed. Talalikhin’s heroic deed forever inscribed his name in world history. For his feat, the legendary Soviet ace was awarded the title of #HeroOfTheSovietUnion , the Order of Lenin and the Gold Star medal. Soon afterwards, the pilot was promoted to a squadron commander — at just 22 years of age — and, later, to the rank of lieutenant. Viktor Talalikhin distinguished himself repeatedly during combat missions, personally bringing down at least four Nazi aircraft and one more as part of a group . He was to destroy a fifth enemy aircraft in his final battle near Podolsk. #FacesOfVictory
🌟
On September 18, 1918, legendary
#WW2
-era Soviet flying ace Viktor Talalikhin was born.
#Talalikhin
entered history thanks to his heroic feat during the
#GreatPatrioticWar
: flying an I-16 fighter, he was among the first ever in history of
#WWII
to carry out an
aerial ramming attack
, bringing down a Nazi Heinkel 'He 111' bomber.
During the fierce aerial battles over Moscow, the young pilot pursued an enemy aircraft, attempting to escape, and directed his I-16 towards a Nazi aircraft tail, opening fire on one of its engines and finally
bringing it down
. Despite sustaining an
injury
, Junior Lieutenant Talalikhin
miraculously survived.
All members of the Luftwaffe bomber crew were killed.
Talalikhin’s heroic deed forever inscribed his name in world history.
For his feat, the legendary Soviet ace was awarded the title of
#HeroOfTheSovietUnion
, the Order of Lenin and the Gold Star medal. Soon afterwards, the pilot was
promoted to a squadron commander
— at just 22 years of age — and, later, to the rank of lieutenant.
Viktor Talalikhin distinguished himself repeatedly during combat missions,
personally bringing down at least four Nazi aircraft and one more as part of a group
. He was to destroy a fifth enemy aircraft in his final battle near Podolsk. Fighting in the skies over the city, Talalikhin was killed in action, yet,
having managed to destroy two Nazi Me-109 fighters.
Against the backdrop of the fierce fighting in the summer of 1941,
Talalikhin’s selfless act
inspired millions.
In total, during WW2, Soviet pilots carried out
more than 600 aerial ramming attacks
against the Germans.
🕯
Viktor Talalikhin was buried with full military honours at Moscow’s Novodevichy Cemetery. The legendary ace was
forever enlisted in the 1st Squadron
of the 177th Fighter Aviation Regiment — that very unit in which he had fought the Nazis in the skies over Moscow.
#Victory81
#WeRemember
#WeAreProud
